title: Implement binary classification precision, recall and F1
instructions: Add a public function binary_classification_metrics(y_true, y_pred, positive_label=1) returning a dictionary with precision, recall, f1, tp, fp, fn and tn. The metric must work for arbitrary hashable labels. When a denominator is zero, return 0.0 for that rate. Reuse existing validation. Export the function through lab/__init__.py and document usage in docs/.
acceptance: Tests cover perfect prediction, false positives, false negatives and zero denominators
Input length mismatch and empty inputs are rejected
All existing tests continue to pass

title: Implement multiclass macro-F1 and per-class metrics
instructions: Implement per_class_metrics(y_true, y_pred), yielding precision, recall, f1 and support for every label found in the inputs, and macro_f1(y_true, y_pred) returning an unweighted average over labels. Use stable predictable label ordering based on first occurrence, not sorting so heterogeneous labels work. Export functions through lab/__init__.py and add docs.
acceptance: Tests cover three-class examples and missing predicted classes
Works for heterogeneous hashable labels without sorting
Empty and mismatched-length inputs are rejected

title: Create a JSON CLI for model metric evaluation
instructions: Add lab/cli.py runnable with python -m lab.cli to accept an input JSON file with y_true and y_pred arrays, calculate accuracy and report available metrics, then output compact JSON to stdout. Return a nonzero exit status and a helpful stderr message for invalid files or data. Document usage. Do not add network access or dependencies.
acceptance: CLI supports a sample JSON file and emits parseable JSON
Invalid file, malformed JSON and mismatched arrays return nonzero exit codes
CLI has tests using subprocess or direct main invocation
